newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel seeks to ease currency control.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel seeks to ease currency control.

text.p: The Bank of Israel plans to ease foreign exchange rate controls "very soon", central bank Governor Jacob Frenkel said on Sunday.
Speaking to Israeli and foreign businessmen, Frenkel said among the government's priorities for the next two to three months was the lowering of exchange rate controls.
"That is practically ready and near and very, very soon," Frenkel said.

Since the late 1980s the central bank has gradually been easing foreign currency controls with the aim of eventually turning the shekel into a free floating currency. But the central bank said this would only occur when inflation reaches levels prevalent in industrialised countries.
Frenkel implied that further foreign exchange liberalisation would be part of a package of measures being worked on jointly by the Treasury and the central bank.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he plans to introduce a package of structural reforms in the economy that would include deregulation and introduction of greater competition.
"There is a very concrete package of economic measures that will be announced jointly, I hope very shortly," Frenkel said.
He said that the lowering of interest rates or a currency devaluation would not be part of any economic package.

Frenkel also stressed the need for quicky passage of the 1997 budget, including 4.9 billion shekels in spending cuts. He said he would not support measures that involved tax hikes rather than budget cuts.
